# Baruch Chapter 3 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/BAR_003_page_001.jpg

---

**1** O Lord Almighty, God of Israel — the soul in agony and the spirit in distress are crying out to you.

**2** Listen, Lord. Have mercy, for you are a God of mercy. Show us compassion, for we have sinned against you.

**3** You sit enthroned forever. We are wasting away.

**4** O Lord Almighty, God of Israel — hear the prayer that rises from the dead of Israel, from the descendants of those who sinned before you, who would not listen to your voice, and now calamity has fastened itself upon us.

**5** Do not hold the sins of our ancestors against us. Remember instead your own power and your name, in this very hour.

**6** For you are the Lord our God, and we will praise you, Lord.

**7** You put your fear into our hearts so that we would call on your name — and we will praise you from this place of exile, for we have stripped away from our hearts all the wickedness our ancestors brought on themselves when they sinned against you.

**8** Here we are today, in this exile where you scattered us — a byword, a curse, subject to punishment for all the sins of our ancestors who turned away from the Lord our God.

**9** Listen, Israel — these are the commandments of life. Open your ears and learn what wisdom is.

**10** What happened to you, Israel? Why are you living in your enemies' land? You have grown old in a foreign country.

**11** You are defiled among the dead. You have been counted with those who descend to Hades.

**12** You walked away from the very spring of wisdom!

**13** If you had walked in God's way, you would be living in peace — forever.

**14** Find out where wisdom is. Find out where strength is, where understanding is. Then you will know where long life is, where the light of your eyes comes from, and where peace lives.

**15** Who has discovered where she dwells? Who has ever entered her treasury?

**16** Where are the rulers of nations now? Where are those who mastered the wild animals of the earth,

**17** those who played games with the birds of heaven, who piled up silver and gold that people trusted in, with never an end to their accumulating —

**18** those who refined silver so carefully, whose work no one could fathom?

**19** They are gone. They went down to Hades. Others have taken their places.

**20** Younger generations came into the light and walked upon the earth — but they never learned the way of wisdom.

**21** They never understood her paths. Their children never received her. She remained far from them.

**22** She was never heard of in Canaan. She was never seen in Teman.

**23** Not the Hagrites who search for understanding across the earth, not the merchants of Merran and Teman, not the storytellers, not those who claim to seek insight — none of them have found the way of wisdom, none have kept her paths in mind.

**24** O Israel — how immense is the house of God! How boundless the territory of his possession!

**25** Vast beyond measure. High beyond reckoning.

**26** The giants were born in that country — the legendary men of old, massive in body and fierce in battle.

**27** But God did not choose them. He did not give them the way of wisdom.

**28** They perished for lack of it. They were destroyed by their own foolishness.

**29** Who has climbed up into heaven and seized wisdom? Who has brought her down out of the clouds?

**30** Who has sailed across the sea and found her? Who could buy her for pure gold?

**31** No one knows the road she travels. No one has worked out her paths.

**32** But the One who knows everything knows her. He found her through his own understanding. The one who established the earth for all time has stocked it with four-footed creatures.

**33** He sends out the light, and off it goes. He calls it back, and it trembles as it obeys.

**34** The stars burn bright in their night watches, full of joy. He calls them — and they answer: "Here we are!" They light up with gladness for the one who made them.

**35** This is our God. No one else comes close.

**36** He found out the whole way of wisdom and gave her to his servant Jacob — to Israel, the one he loved.

**37** After that, she appeared on the earth. She came and lived among human beings.

**38** She is the book of God's commandments, the law that lasts forever. Everyone who holds on to her will live. Everyone who abandons her will die.

---
*PNEUMA notes: v.37 is the hinge-verse of the entire chapter and arguably one of the most theologically charged sentences in all the Deuterocanon. In context, "she" is Wisdom personified, and v.38 clarifies that this Wisdom is identified with Torah. Yet the language — "she appeared on the earth and came and lived among human beings" — is startlingly incarnational. Early Christian readers (Justin, Clement, Origen, Irenaeus) consistently read this as a prophecy of Christ. Whether or not that was the author's intent, the verse stands at the intersection of Jewish Wisdom theology and the prologue of John's Gospel (John 1:14: "the Word became flesh and dwelt among us"). PNEUMA has rendered it with maximum clarity and minimum paraphrase: "she appeared on the earth. She came and lived among human beings." The bifurcation into two sentences marks the verse's gravity without overcrowding it.*
